scope: Documented capabilities and explicitly qualified scale evidence; not implementation certification

columns.title: PRP L3
columns.profile: PRP wire-v4, protected adjacency and E2E 0x0101; local bootstrap, known identities; privacy mechanisms enabled; C08: interior transit between intermediaries, no endpoint rendezvous/deeper-session termination or optional traffic-history logging

columns.title: PRP over IP
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / PRP wire-v4, protected adjacency and E2E 0x0101; numeric peers, known identities; privacy mechanisms enabled; independent deployment uses private IPv4; C08: interior transit between intermediaries, no endpoint rendezvous/deeper-session termination or optional traffic-history logging G01 global deployment: conventional globally routed IPv4/UDP over the BGP Internet, matching IP/MQ and round119 BP/LP/I2/GN. Private IPv4 deployments remain separate S03 capabilities; adjacent-only IP meshes are not this global witness. This does not change native PRP L3.

columns.title: IP (IPv4/IPv6)
columns.profile: IPv4 or IPv6 datagram service / ICMP; numeric destinations; no application TCP/UDP/TLS/QUIC or IPsec, NAT or stateful firewall; optional transit traffic-history/export disabled. Global unicast control: TCP / BGP-4 + MP-BGP. F12: IGMP/MLD + PIM-SM. Independent deployment: RFC 1918 private IPv4 or locally generated IPv6 ULA, locally provisioned routes. Global Internet allocation remains a separate requirement. F09: optional per-packet unicast next-hop rotation over provisioned multiple routes (RFC 2991), not merely flow-hashed ECMP; G04: multiple BGP reflector clusters and group-scoped PIM RPs.; C06: separate IPv6 client contexts with distinct randomized temporary sources under a shared multi-host prefix, no stable source/DNS identity or host-identifying flow-label policy reused; no continuity or on-link anonymity claim

columns.title: Secure DTN
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS 1.3 / TCPCLv4 / BPv7 + BPSec; independent private IPv4 and RFC 9758 private-use ipn domain; known EIDs, aggregate gateway exits, locally agreed dtn collective names, numeric peers; participant-operated CAs, local trust and BPSec keys, NODE-ID validation, no online OCSP or SNI; optional TLS padding, concurrent proactive forwarding and static collective fanout credited architecturally; independent logical-node EIDs/certificates/BPSec keys per context, no cross-context TLS resumption; discard completed bundles, no retained report archive or transit traffic history G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching the IP/MQ global case; private deployments remain separate S03 capabilities. F21: ION native BPSec receive-API witness at 154a4cc7354b26661169f8d8b75a4002cd509a9f; exact source-EID/key bindings, distinct pairwise HMAC keys held only by each original sender and receiver, BIBs over primary and payload, primary-inclusive payload integrity scope; application treats bundleSourceEid as authenticated only when both native verification indicators are true. No application authentication exchange, group key or relay-held origin key; no F16 admission/revocation guarantee inferred. F16 alternative witness: ION 154a4cc with optional BSL 468db9b enabled and mandatory APPOUT wildcard-source BIB verification over primary and payload. One authorized remote sender at a time; a fresh secret key is held only by that sender and the final receiver, never transit. Native policy uses a locally fixed key-registry identifier. Revocation uses completed shutdown of receiver and consumers, a fresh empty bundle/fragment/delivery store and a fresh key provisioned only to the newly authorized sender. No hot revocation, simultaneous independent-key allowlist, or claimed source-EID authentication is inferred from this witness; F21 retains its separate exact-source policy.

columns.title: DTN / CGR–SABR
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS 1.3 / TCPCLv4 / BPv7 + BPSec, with CGR routing procedures from SABR CCSDS 734.3-B-1 (2019). Documentary composition; executable integration not yet qualified. Locally provisioned numeric peers, private IPv4, private-use ipn identifiers (RFC 9758), singleton destinations, supplied contact/range plans and local clocks. Participant-operated certificate trust with NODE-ID validation, no online OCSP, DNS or SNI dependency. Final-pair BCB-AES-GCM payload protection and BIB-HMAC-SHA2 verification with locally provisioned pairwise keys; no relay-held final keys. No application authentication wrapper, anonymity overlay, multicast extension or shared-reference directory. BPv7 mapping of SABR priority/critical metadata and custody-dependent behavior remains an explicit integration question, not silently credited.

columns.title: DTN / LTP
columns.profile: BPv7 + BPSec / LTP RFC 5326 / Encapsulation Packet Protocol 133.1-B-3 / AOS virtual-channel packet service 732.0-B-4 (2021 documentary baseline, not latest edition); CGR/SABR 734.3-B-1 routing. LTP segment binding follows 734.1-B-1 Annex B. No UDP, IP, TCPCL or TLS. Bidirectional adjacent links, locally supplied contact/range plans, peer/engine mapping, clocks and keys; singleton BP endpoints. All-red block transfer selected; optional green-part service is not credited. Final-pair BCB-AES-GCM and BIB-HMAC-SHA2 protect payload and authenticate a configured remote security source; no relay-held final keys. No link encryption/SDLS, anonymity overlay, application authentication wrapper or independent-participant discovery directory. Executable bindings, BPv7/SABR metadata mapping and allocation rules remain unqualified. CCSDS mission conformance and unrestricted local engine/channel assignment are not asserted.

columns.title: libp2p
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / QUIC (TLS 1.3) / libp2p; known numeric peers and Peer IDs, migration enabled; independent deployment uses private IPv4; separate logical peer keys/stores per context, no resumption, NAT or transit flow logging; no pubsub F16: final Peer ID allowlist through ConnectionGater plus coordinated closure of all revoked-peer connections. G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching the IP/MQ global case; private deployments remain separate S03 capabilities.

columns.title: Tor onion service
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS / Tor + onion service v3; public Tor directory system; persistent filesystem client authorization enabled; transit traffic-history logging disabled; optional Conflux proposal-329 onion-service linking/resumption credited as design, not verified deployment; F21: client identity delivered to the receiving onion service; reverse service authentication is distinct F16: authorization-file removal plus Tor restart; retain authorization for permitted clients or stop the service when none remain.

columns.title: I2P
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / NTCP2 / I2P destinations and tunnels; locally supplied fresh RouterInfo bundle, numeric NTCP2 contacts and known destination keys; multiple active outbound tunnels with at least two remote hops, tunneled destination lookups; correct local clock; no online reseed or external naming service; isolated router/destination key contexts without shared family declarations; independent private IPv4 with i2np.allowLocal and local bootstrap/network configuration; concurrent-tunnel policy is architectural, ordinary Java per-pair selection is sticky; transit-only C08 role with optional identity-bearing traffic/debug history disabled G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching the IP/MQ global case; private deployments remain separate S03 capabilities.

columns.title: Yggdrasil
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS 1.3 / Yggdrasil / IPv6 / application UDP; optional TLS padding credited architecturally; numeric peers, pinned keys, numeric application destinations; independent deployment uses private IPv4; independent logical-node keys and TLS contexts, no cross-context resumption; transit traffic-history logging/export disabled; ordinary TCP only, no MPTCP or custom scheduler; Ironwood pinned to d50055b11f5ec5b56ee4e56ba9a75261461821dc; G01: connected mesh of adjacent-only private-IP peerings, no Internet transit or remote public peers; F21: applications on native node addresses, not devices behind routed subnets; trusted local receive interface

columns.title: cjdns
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / cjdns / IPv6 / application UDP; ordinary application path without custom route-label overrides; outer point-to-point CryptoAuth enabled; numeric peers, known keys/local credentials, numeric application destinations; independent deployment uses private IPv4; independent logical-node keys and non-identifying peer credentials per context; transit traffic-history logging/export disabled; C02 includes documented DHT lookup role; no selected cover-traffic policy; private peering credentials, no public beacon advertisement; replicated route-server design with TCP/HTTP/WebSocket announcement exchange, independent servers and numeric contacts; C08 covers transit forwarding, not route-server query caches; F21: applications on native cryptographic node addresses, no imported IP tunnels; trusted local receive interface

columns.title: Multipath QUIC
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / QUIC (TLS 1.3) + multipath-21, optional proactive same-offset STREAM copies on two validated paths; numeric peers, locally generated certificates explicitly trusted by counterparts, mutual handshake authentication, no SNI requirement or online certificate service; independent private IPv4 deployment; separate trusted context keys, no cross-context tickets/token reuse, NAT or transit flow logging F16: local final-key allowlist, all-connection close on revocation, resumption and 0-RTT disabled.; G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay; private deployment remains a separate S03 capability

columns.title: SCION
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP underlay / SCION / application UDP; numeric topology, daemon, control/discovery and endpoint addresses, locally provisioned trust and correct local clock; no end-to-end TLS; independent UDP end-host address/flow contexts within an AS; transit traffic-history logging/export disabled

columns.title: Reticulum
columns.profile: Reticulum 1.5.5 / Link over serial interfaces; secret IFAC enabled, credentials not publicly advertised; no local TCP sharing or IP interfaces; no LXMF; regional transport-node distribution; no application cover-traffic policy; F21: native Link.identify enabled; identity-dependent actions wait for verified identification; G01: connected serial mesh with recursive_prs enabled on transport interfaces C08: Reticulum 1.5.5 standalone serial transport with the entire --config directory on private verified noswap tmpfs; no host swap/hibernation/dumps, snapshots, durable logs or exporters. Seed only clean static config/local identity/IFAC credentials; do not restore learned paths, announces or participant activity. Cold starts relearn routes. This supersedes the earlier C08 stock-disk profile; RAM activity remains observable.

columns.title: Basic Nostr
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS 1.3 / HTTP Upgrade / WebSocket / NIP-01; optional TLS padding credited architecturally; WSS relay hostnames resolved through DNS; regular events proactively published concurrently over two independent relay paths; separate author contexts; no NIP-17/44/42 or secret-gated camouflage; F21: verified event author to reader, not live publishing connection or relay identity; G01 global deployment: WSS relays over conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet C08: operator-controlled nostr-rs-relay at b5c1f642e4f4c3b9c54f5d18d66f4c53642076b4, SQLite in_memory=true, bundled URI-enabled SQLite and memory temporary storage; no file logging, persistent WSS-proxy logs, diagnostics export, swap, dumps, hibernation or snapshots. Apply to both selected relays. Regular events remain in RAM until discarded/restart; other readers/relays can retain copies.

columns.title: Meshtastic
columns.profile: Meshtastic firmware v2.8.1.8e6a88d Alpha (commit 8e6a88d06f44cad26f1e8d7cd402939ccacb9b4c); standalone LoRa mesh, radio/region preset agreed locally, ordinary CLIENT relaying; no MQTT, Wi-Fi/Ethernet network or Internet bridge; trusted local serial client. PKI-capable build, direct messages with independently confirmed endpoint public keys; private channel key, STRICT signature policy, no licensed plaintext mode. Store-and-forward module disabled. No claim that this Alpha is a production recommendation; radio nodes are the cryptographic endpoints. C04 witness fixes ordinary CLIENT rebroadcast_mode=ALL; private-channel key and STRICT signature policy retained. Unknown-channel opaque forwarding is included, not CLIENT_MUTE/NONE. F16 administrative witness: headless CLIENT, KNOWN_ONLY plus STRICT, locally provisioned authorized User records/full keys only, no remote administrative authority for ordinary peers; store-forward off, persisted ignore policy and completed restart for revocation. Separate from C04 CLIENT/ALL probe witness. C06 witness: native meshtasticd/Portduino with real LoRa radio, separately provisioned full contexts, explicit distinct General.MACAddress values, independent keys/names/preferences and no shared identifier-bearing telemetry. No automatic embedded-device rotation claim or UDP radio transport. C08: native Linux meshtasticd with real SPI/USB LoRa, ordinary CLIENT/ALL relaying, full writable virtual filesystem on verified private tmpfs with noswap; host swap/hibernation/dumps and persistent log/export/backup paths disabled. Restore only clean static identity/radio/trust provisioning at cold start, never learned NodeDB/history. No flash-device default or live-memory secrecy claim.

columns.title: GNUnet / CADET
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP TRANSPORT plugin / CORE / CADET; R5N discovery. GNUnet v0.20.x handbook is the explicit documentary baseline, not a claim about the latest release. Numeric private-IP neighbors, locally supplied HELLO contacts and known peer public keys; no online hostlist, DNS, NAT helper, GNS, file-sharing or Messenger service. Runtime version and discovery/bootstrap configuration remain to be qualified. G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching the IP/MQ global case; private deployments remain separate S03 capabilities. C08 witness: GNUnet 0.20.0 legacy UDP, proportional ATS, heap dhtcache with DISABLE_BF_RC=YES, peerinfo NO_IO=YES, logging NONE without forced overrides; fresh service state, no optional traffic archive/TNG, bootstrap contacts supplied again after restart. F16 witness: dedicated CADET endpoint with no local listening ports; locally initiated bidirectional channels only to an administratively selected set of peer public keys. Revocation uses a completed cold restart of the local CADET service and its consuming clients, discarding old channel/IPC delivery state before recreating channels only to the updated set. No application payload validator, external firewall or incoming-channel acceptance callback is credited. This is a controlled receiver/subscriber configuration, not an incoming server allowlist or uninterrupted hot revocation.

columns.title: NDN / NFD
columns.profile: NDN packet format v0.3 / NFD 24.07 with direct Ethernet faces and local Unix-socket applications; no IP face, DNS discovery or public testbed enrollment. Known content/key names, local FIB configuration and local trust anchors; ECDSA P-256 Data signatures validated by the consumer. No content-encryption extension, mandatory signed consumer Interests, application sync/group protocol or DTN extension. Data-producer authentication is distinct from live peer authentication. F18 witness: positive-capacity CS with admission/serving enabled, solicited staged cache transfers, bounded contacts before eviction/freshness expiry; no custody or restart durability claim. G01 witness: connected tree of direct Ethernet adjacencies; native multicast v5 strategy at /, root-prefix next hops to every neighbor, and local producer registrations only. Known globally scoped names, no forwarding hints, NLSR, global directory or IP underlay. Interest lifetime/hop budget covers the tree diameter; provision resources for the offered load. This flooding construction establishes reachability, not G05 capacity or efficient routing.

columns.title: AX.25 / NET/ROM
columns.profile: AX.25 v2 / classic NET/ROM network and transport circuits over direct radio/serial links; known callsigns/SSIDs, locally configured routing ports and NET/ROM announcements. Historical protocol description plus Linux AX.25 port configuration; no IP encapsulation, TCP/IP payload service, BBS mailbox or added cryptography. Executable version not yet qualified. S01/S03/C06 credit the private direct-serial role with locally provisioned labels; no claim about radio licensing or public callsign acceptance.

columns.title: batman-adv
columns.profile: Linux 6.12 batman-adv / native Ethernet frame service, direct Ethernet-style links; no IP application, VPN underlay, WPA/MACsec or end-to-end security layer. Locally administered MAC addresses, local interface attachment and trusted local client; This is an L2 service boundary, not an IP application stack. Round118 witnesses: BATMAN_IV, native bonding enabled for F09, gateway mode off, network coding not credited; shared-code IV/V findings identified per cell.

columns.title: IP / Babel
columns.profile: IPv6 datagram service / ICMPv6; control plane IPv6 / UDP / Babel RFC 8966. Independent locally assigned ULA prefixes, provisioned interfaces, numeric destinations; no DNS, TCP/QUIC, IPsec, NAT, external firewall, Babel DTLS/MAC extension or added application authentication. Babel is the selected routing control plane; no BGP/global Internet composition silently added. G01 constructive witness: administratively provisioned binary IPv6 hierarchy inside a locally assigned ULA /48, with direct routed adjacencies. Each router originates only its own aggregate backed by a local discard route; upward advertisements contain that aggregate, downward advertisements only the root /48. Exact-prefix/interface input and output filters suppress remote specifics. Connected leaf LANs override their local aggregate. No BGP, directory, automatic aggregation controller or global leaf-prefix catalog is introduced. Fixed hierarchy and address assignment are required; this is not arbitrary Internet topology or G05 capacity.

criteria.title: Operates without IPv4/IPv6 throughout the stack
criteria.definition: No mandatory IP layer, including operational support.
criteria.research_action: Fix non-IP binding, bootstrap and support dependencies; run without IP.

criteria.title: Needs no participant IP address configuration
criteria.definition: Participant-facing addressing uses a self-generated address or a non-IP participant namespace; no assigned participant IP address is needed at that layer. Underlay and relay transport IP configuration are excluded uniformly and remain assessed by F01/F03. This is not zero-configuration deployment: other identifiers, peers, trust and permissions may need provisioning.
criteria.research_action: Trace endpoint creation and bootstrap; distinguish application and underlay configuration.

criteria.title: Routed operation needs no topology-dependent address configuration
criteria.definition: No network-prefix, subnet or locator assignment tied to attachment in the selected stack, including its underlay. DHCP/SLAAC automate such configuration rather than remove it. Locally generated identities and session-local forwarding labels do not count. Excludes route policy, trust, permissions and physical/link setup.
criteria.research_action: Trace address assignment across the selected stack; distinguish topology-dependent locators from self-generated identities and local forwarding labels. F02 concerns participant provisioning; F03 concerns the routed network as a whole.

criteria.title: Cryptographic reference independent of location
criteria.definition: Participant or service reference verifiable independently of its locator; not necessarily self-certifying.
criteria.research_action: Trace reference creation and key binding; distinguish identity, certificate and locator.

criteria.title: Persistent relationship as an architectural object
criteria.definition: Continuity and authorization context independent of session and carrier lifetimes.
criteria.research_action: Find an equivalent continuity and authorization contract; a stable key alone is insufficient.

criteria.title: Encrypts content between communicating endpoints
criteria.definition: Protection between the compared endpoints, not merely a transit link.
criteria.research_action: Fix the end-to-end profile and key custody; identify every encryption termination point.

criteria.title: Cryptographically authenticates a remote participant
criteria.definition: Remote identity or signed authorship proof; does not imply civil identity, mutual authentication or current presence.
criteria.research_action: Specify whose identity is proved, to whom, and whether proof covers a live session or stored message.

criteria.title: Preserves a transport connection across path changes
criteria.definition: The same connection survives; reconnecting with the same contact does not qualify. UDP alone has no connection.
criteria.research_action: Define address/path change and connection lifetime; test continuity, replay and reordering.

criteria.title: Uses simultaneous paths for one communication
criteria.definition: Concurrent useful data paths, rather than sequential failover or probes.
criteria.research_action: Fix scheduler, path policy and extension; distinguish multiple sessions from one communication.

criteria.title: Proactively duplicates data across distinct paths
criteria.definition: Intentional redundancy before loss, rather than retransmission after loss.
criteria.research_action: Find replication and deduplication rules; test physically diverse paths and resource costs.

criteria.title: Retains messages for delivery after disconnection
criteria.definition: Deferred delivery storage, not transient transport buffers.
criteria.research_action: Check persistence, expiry, capacity and recovery without a contemporaneous path.

criteria.title: Multicast replication at network forwarders
criteria.definition: One-to-many network forwarding; application-relay fanout does not qualify. BP selects static collective fanout with implementation qualification pending.
criteria.research_action: Fix multicast routing and replication; distinguish broadcast, flooding and application pubsub.

criteria.title: Groupcast with PRP-equivalent semantics
criteria.definition: Multiple senders with distributed group authority and continuity; matching terminology is insufficient.
criteria.research_action: Compare membership, authority, continuity, multiple senders and distribution semantics.

criteria.title: Explicit goal of concealing endpoint location
criteria.definition: Location-hiding mechanism; not immunity to global correlation.
criteria.research_action: Define observer and profile; inventory visible identity, adjacency and location metadata.

criteria.title: Isolates resources under distributed DoS
criteria.definition: Preserves specified minimum legitimate service under a bounded adversary.
criteria.research_action: Fix adversary budget and bottlenecks; measure admission, goodput, latency, CPU, memory and queues.

criteria.title: Controls final-peer access without external firewall
criteria.definition: Final-peer network payload admission: allow locally authorized cryptographic peers, deny others before application payload delivery, and revoke old authority at a completed local cutover, including active paths and pending delivery. Native policy hooks and administrative teardown/restart are allowed; authorized service must remain available after cutover. Already delivered data, application-operation permissions, handshake/probe traffic, unrelated host services and DoS isolation are outside scope. Added application authentication or payload filtering is not credited.
criteria.research_action: Trace native final-peer admission and revocation at completed local cutover; see round063.html#policy.

criteria.title: Operates without DNS
criteria.definition: No DNS from bootstrap through authorized traffic; names absent from packets alone are insufficient.
criteria.research_action: Fix peers, discovery, certificates and dependencies; initialize without DNS queries.

criteria.title: DTN forwarding across discontinuous contacts
criteria.definition: Network intermediaries retain and later forward an admitted item across non-overlapping contacts, without a contemporaneous complete end-to-end path. A mailbox at a common server, transport buffering or reconnection alone does not qualify. Previously established trust and bounded expiry are allowed.
criteria.research_action: Trace A-to-B followed by B-to-C with no overlapping contacts, intermediate storage, expiry, cryptographic viability and duplicate handling; distinguish architecture from executable activation.

criteria.title: Transit forwarding without per-end-to-end-flow state
criteria.definition: Transit can forward without a mandatory entry for each end-to-end flow or circuit. Routes, neighbor sessions and aggregate multicast state are allowed. Endpoint transport state is outside this transit-only test. Include selected overlay relays, not only the IP underlay.
criteria.research_action: Inventory every selected transit role and its state keys/lifetimes. Distinguish aggregate routes and neighbor sessions from endpoint-flow/circuit entries and optional caches.

criteria.title: Authenticated final-peer identity available to the application
criteria.definition: The selected stack authenticates the final communicating peer and exposes that identity to the receiving application bound to the communication, without an added application authentication exchange. Neighbor identity, unauthenticated addresses or an unbound claim are insufficient. This does not supply civil identity, account roles, permissions or transit anonymity.
criteria.research_action: Trace proof validation, application-visible identity and binding to the received channel/item. Separate final peer from relays, object authors and security sources; inspect close/rekey and stale-reference behavior.

criteria.title: Shared-reference discovery of independent participants
criteria.definition: One shared reference can discover multiple independently identified participants, without an exclusive controller of that reference or a shared private identity. A bounded candidate set is sufficient; exhaustive enumeration and simultaneous delivery are not required. Only mechanisms in the declared stack count. Self-declaration does not establish membership legitimacy, service authorization or current availability.
criteria.research_action: Trace reference formation, independent declarations, multi-candidate lookup and candidate identity binding. Separate routing fanout, anycast and content retrieval from participant discovery; do not silently add a discovery application or module.

criteria.title: Endpoint mobility without infrastructure routing control
criteria.definition: Supports an endpoint changing attachment or access network while preserving its peer identity and ongoing logical communication, without requiring the application to establish a new peer relationship or reconstruct communication. The endpoint must not need administrative control of infrastructure routes, prefix origination or an AS; moving an administratively controlled network with the endpoint does not qualify. Normal participant attachment, path authentication and automatic protocol signaling are allowed, including signaling intrinsic to a mesh or overlay; merely running routing code does not disqualify a participant. Ordinary network access permission is not authority to originate infrastructure routes. Evaluate a supported endpoint role and state its limits; client-only support can qualify. Mere route repair with stationary endpoints, or retaining an identifier while restarting communication, is insufficient. Lossless handover, simultaneous mobility of both endpoints and indefinite disconnection are not required. Only mechanisms in the declared stack count.
criteria.research_action: Move an ordinary participant between attachments with no new infrastructure route/prefix/AS privileges. Trace retained identity and communication state, automatic locator/path updates and application-visible behavior. List access permissions separately from routing authority. Exclude administrator-driven prefix/AS relocation. Record role, interruption, loss and timeout; test existing runtime qualifications separately.

criteria.title: Recovers after one path is blocked
criteria.definition: One operator drops a path; another reachable, authorized path has capacity. Reconnection and interruption are permitted.
criteria.research_action: Block one laboratory path; measure recovery, loss and discovery dependence on that path.

criteria.title: Conceals the final destination from the first intermediary
criteria.definition: A non-colluding intermediary sees its decrypted state and traffic. Excludes direct endpoint communication.
criteria.research_action: Inventory keys, fields, control queries and forwarding tables; check final identity and location exposure.

criteria.title: Conceals protocol control fields in established traffic
criteria.definition: Passive observation of established protected traffic, excluding bootstrap. Assess exposed control fields and protocol markers; timing/volume inference is separate. This is not a claim of complete protocol indistinguishability.
criteria.research_action: Map cleartext and encrypted established-packet fields, including outer framing; do not use initial bootstrap exposure as a negative.

criteria.title: Includes a defense against active-probe identification
criteria.definition: An uncredentialed adversary probes an endpoint and observes replies and timing; no endpoint compromise.
criteria.research_action: Define valid, invalid and replay probes; inspect disclosures before authorization against a control service.

criteria.title: Bootstraps while external DNS is unavailable
criteria.definition: Initial state as specified in the column, with no DNS cache. Does not cover blocking all peers or directories.
criteria.research_action: Disable DNS before process startup; inventory discovery and trust. F17 is the corresponding functional capability.

criteria.title: Includes access-level cross-session unlinkability
criteria.definition: Capability to avoid a compulsory persistent participant-identity link across sessions. Excludes bootstrap, known subscriber attachment and timing/volume inference. Optional identity reuse does not negate the capability.
criteria.research_action: Identify stable identifiers and support for distinct identities across contexts; distinguish a compulsory identity link from user-selected reuse and timing inference.

criteria.title: Includes a defense against entry/exit correlation
criteria.definition: Includes a mechanism that reduces observable timing/volume information for cooperating observers. Optional padding or cover traffic can qualify; effectiveness and deployment defaults are separate, and complete correlation prevention is not required.
criteria.research_action: Identify padding, batching, mix or cover mechanisms and their scope; separately measure correlation reduction and cost under a fixed observer model.

criteria.title: Needs no persistent history of final identities
criteria.definition: A transit operator or relay supplies stored state after communication. Capability requires operation without persistent author/destination history.
criteria.research_action: Inspect memory, disk, backups, telemetry and default logs; separate required, optional and derivable data. This is not a legal retention ruling.

criteria.title: Protocol sovereignty: no mandatory external authority
criteria.definition: Willing peers can communicate from local information without a separate mandatory naming, routing, identity, governance or ledger authority. Network directory authorities and domain certification roles count; counterpart admission policies do not. Underlay allocation is assessed separately.
criteria.research_action: Identify any indispensable third-party approval, registry, consensus signer or trust anchor in the selected network. Test direct operation without that external service.

criteria.title: Participant identity requires no external issuer
criteria.definition: Participants generate a usable cryptographic identity locally; counterparties decide whether to trust or authorize it. Does not imply civil identity.
criteria.research_action: Trace key creation, reference registration and acceptance; determine whether an issuer must authorize creation.

criteria.title: Selected stack needs no external address/name allocation
criteria.definition: Independent deployment needs no public address allocation, DNS delegation or externally assigned domain identifier. Private/local addressing may qualify; Internet reachability is a separate requirement.
criteria.research_action: Fix deployment boundary, private/public underlay and name resolution; inventory allocator and delegation dependencies.

criteria.title: Global reachability without complete global reachability tables
criteria.definition: The complete selected stack permits global reachability without requiring a complete global reachability table at transit nodes or control services. Include prefix, identity and other identifier reachability, and required underlay routing. Moving that table upstream or into a directory does not qualify. Partitioned state is allowed; this is not zero state or a quantitative capacity guarantee.
criteria.research_action: Inventory every transit and control role, including discovery, upper aggregators and the underlay. Establish how arbitrary reachable destinations are located without a mandatory complete global table. A local default route, local labels or a small private deployment alone are insufficient.

criteria.title: Local repair without mandatory global dissemination
criteria.definition: A documented local attachment change can be repaired within an affected scope without notifying every node. Not a guarantee for every failure.
criteria.research_action: Trace local repair and propagation, including underlay; identify cases requiring wider updates.

criteria.title: Discovery without a complete catalog at every node
criteria.definition: Scoped services or recursive queries permit discovery without a global catalog at every node. Does not bound rendezvous or backbone costs.
criteria.research_action: Trace cold lookup, state placement, publication updates and cache-miss fanout.

criteria.title: Scale-out without a fixed-capacity coordination point
criteria.definition: Added infrastructure can distribute routing/discovery work without an obligatory single fixed-capacity coordinator. Decentralization alone is insufficient.
criteria.research_action: Map complete-stack coordination dependencies, partitioning, replication and failure recovery.

criteria.title: Global scale with bounded discovery and overhead
criteria.definition: One connected network of at least 10 billion devices on contemporary equipment, evaluated in an agreed reference deployment calibrated to regional Internet interconnections and participant concentration. Existing destinations unknown to the origin: protocol-attributable discovery delay below 1 s; new participants discoverable across regions within 1 h. At least 99.9% of attempts meet deadlines, counting failures/timeouts. Control and unsolicited traffic below 5% of a 1 Gbit/s domestic access per direction. Required routing state below 64 GB per transit equipment, not per endpoint; distributed state and growing aggregate network memory are allowed, without a mandatory complete participant table at any one equipment. Include all required stack layers and declared load, ingress and mobility. At least 1,000 distinct destinations accessed per device per day, independently of concurrent payload activity; cold-origin and warm-cache cohorts must be explicit. See round174.html.
criteria.method: Model and validation against approved operational limits
criteria.research_action: Validate the approved limits simultaneously under declared cross-region workloads. Keep protocol processing, queueing, timers, retries and extra exchanges in discovery delay; subtract only a preregistered minimal physical-medium baseline and report total elapsed time too. Count all routing-essential structures per transit equipment across processes. No global monetary or aggregate-memory ceiling.
